subject: Commit phasing, fallback credits & tier summary
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@bluegridhealth.com>, BlueGrid Rev Ops <revops@bluegridhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Initial commit framework for BlueGrid - starter/growth/enterprise

Hi Asha / Rev Ops team,

Thanks for the call earlier — appreciated the clarity on your 2027 roadmap and the peak inference windows you expect in Q1/Q2. Per our discussion I attached a concise commit summary that lays out three annual tiers and a recommended phasing approach. High level:

- Starter: 50M tokens/year (good for small feature rollouts)
- Growth: 500M tokens/year (production features across 3 apps)
- Enterprise: 2B tokens/year (high-volume + dedicated capacity credits)

A few things to note up front: pricing below is usage-based with per-token rates that scale by tier; we support monthly ramping within the year and a limited rollover of unused commitment into Q1 of the next year. We also offer a fallback/overage protection credit model so you don’t get hit with unpredictable bills during spikes — I called this out in the attachment.

Attached: 20260805_commit_summary.xlsx (tier math + sample invoices) and a one-page SOW draft. Can you confirm which tier you want to pilot in H1? If helpful, we can propose a 3-month phased ramp (25% / 50% / 25% of annual nominal tokens across the first three months) to smooth invoices.

Next steps: if you confirm the target tier and preferred ramp profile we’ll (a) lock the per-token rates, (b) create a paperwork bundle for legal and (c) map monthly invoice examples for your FP&A.

Thanks,
Maya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Initial commit framework for BlueGrid - starter/growth/enterprise

Maya — thanks for this, looks thoughtful. Quick questions from our side:

1) Our usage pattern is bursty around monthly billing closes (both dev and production). How do you handle spikes relative to the committed volume — is there an overage rate, or do you offer credits we can pull from?
2) Rollover: you mentioned limited rollover — what % of unused tokens move forward and what are the timing constraints?
3) For Starter, can we do a shorter trial-ish commit (6 months) instead of annual to validate latency/cost before we commit to a full year?

If you can add the overage/credit language and an example invoice showing a 3x spike month, that would help. Also looping in our Rev Ops to make sure the billing cadence is clear.

—Asha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@bluegridhealth.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 04 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial commit framework for BlueGrid - starter/growth/enterprise — pricing + fallback mechanics

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear questions. I’m Marissa (Head of Revenue Operations); looping in Ben (pricing) and Neha (customer success) for ops/readiness notes. Below is a consolidated, actionable proposal that addresses spikes, rollover, and a 6-month Starter option. I also attached a CSV that shows line-by-line math.

Proposal (annual commitment examples and mechanics):

1) Pricing tiers (annual commit / effective per-token rate / typical discount)
- Starter: 50,000,000 tokens/year — $0.0042 / token (approx 12% off list) — suitable for narrow pilots
- Growth: 500,000,000 tokens/year — $0.0032 / token (approx 24% off list) — production multi-app
- Enterprise: 2,000,000,000 tokens/year — $0.0023 / token (approx 35% off list) + optional Dedicated Capacity Credit (applies as $/hour credit toward reserved pool)

2) Phasing & ramping (default and optional)
- Default annual starts: equalized monthly allocation (annual_commit/12).
- Pilot phasing (recommended): 3-month ramp = 25% / 50% / 25% of the quarterly target for initial production launch. This prevents large early overprovisioning and reduces unused commitment.
- 6-month Starter option: we can do a 6-month min-commit at 50% of the annual Starter price (billed prorated) with the same effective per-token rate applied to usage — after 6 months you can convert to annual with a true-up.

3) Spike / overage handling and fallback credits
- Overage rate: usage beyond committed tokens billed at 1.6x the per-token rate for the tier (example in CSV).
- Fallback credit: for any single monthly spike that exceeds committed monthly allocation by > 50% we will: (a) apply a pooled fallback credit equal to 25% of that month’s overage charge, capped at $10k per incident for Starter, $50k for Growth, $200k for Enterprise OR (b) allow short-term burst coverage by using pre-purchased token credits at a blended rate — customer choice at time of spike.
- Rollover: up to 10% of unused annual committed tokens can roll into the first quarter of next year; unused beyond that expires. This preserves predictability for capacity planning.

4) Invoice visibility and sample impact
- We created a month-by-month sample (in the attached spreadsheet) that shows nominal monthly invoice under equalized allocation vs. a 3x spike month and the net with fallback credit applied.

5) Next steps / paperwork
- If BlueGrid confirms a target tier + phasing (and whether you want the 6-month Starter option), we’ll send a commercial term sheet + SOW for legal review and a PO-ready invoice. We can also prepare a one-page FP&A view showing monthly cash impact for your finance team.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/BlueGrid_7392

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet.

—Marissa

Marissa / Maya — this is helpful and answers most of our concerns. A few quick items before we loop in procurement and legal: 

- We like the Growth tier math and the fallback credit language — please add an explicit example line in the SOW that shows how the fallback credit would be applied (simple numbers, e.g., committed monthly = 41.7M tokens, spike month usage = 125M tokens).
- For Starter, can you change the 6-month trial so that it bills as 30% of the annual Starter commitment (instead of 50%) — it lowers our upfront payment and we’ll true-up at conversion. If you can confirm that change we can move to paperwork.
- Please include a one-page FP&A view showing monthly cash impact under the proposed 3-month phased ramp and the equalized allocation model (per your attachment). We’ll share with our CFO.
